title: One run across five repos: routes, users, the merge, and what fell out of it.

features.name: Payment routes
features.assumes: Nothing. This is the base layer.
features.exposes: `POST /routes` returns a route with `providerId` and `settlementDelay`. Everything above reads those two fields.
features.chose: One shared route table over per-provider tables. Faster to ship, and unwinding it now means a migration.

features.name: Users tab
features.assumes: A user record carries `providerId` from payment routes.
features.exposes: User list and role assignment. Roles are a string on the user row.
features.chose: Roles on the user record over a permissions service. Holds until someone needs two roles at once.

features.name: Merge: routes + users
features.exposes: Route visibility is gated on user role. This is the join everything above depends on.
features.chose: Merged users into routes, not the reverse - users already read the route shape, so routes stayed the stable side.

features.name: Application pending actions
features.assumes: The role-gated route list from the merge. Reads `settlementDelay` to decide what counts as pending.
features.exposes: A pending-action queue the mobile app polls.
features.chose: Polling over push. Cheap now, will need replacing at volume.

features.name: Payout webhooks
features.assumes: `settlementDelay` is a fixed number per provider.
features.exposes: Nothing. Reverted five days after shipping.
features.chose: Retried on provider timeout, which double-charged async providers. The assumption from the base layer does not hold for them, and this map is the only place that link is written down.

features.name: End-to-end coverage
features.assumes: Everything below is stable enough to assert against.
features.exposes: A suite that fails loudly when any assumption above changes.
features.chose: Covering the merge seam first, not the leaves.

features.name: Notification preferences
features.assumes: The pending-action queue keeps its current shape.

decisions.chose: Treat settlementDelay as a fixed number per provider
decisions.over: reading it from the provider on every call
decisions.because: Every consumer wanted a number it could cache.
decisions.cost: Async providers have no fixed delay, and nothing above knows that.
decisions.note: Payout webhooks retried on timeout and double-charged async providers. The map is the only place this traces back to the base layer.

decisions.because: Faster to ship in one run.
decisions.cost: Unwinding it now means a migration.

decisions.chose: Roles as a string on the user record
decisions.cost: Holds until someone needs two roles at once.
